purpose: Practical-identifiability and time-respecting validation diagnostic for the monetary-policy to lending-rate partial-adjustment mechanism.

source.policy_rate_context: NBR Annual Report 2023 states the policy rate remained 7.00 percent through the first half of 2024; the January 2025 bulletin records 6.75 in July and 6.50 from August 2024 onward.

definitions.policy_rate_pct: NBR policy rate, end of period, percent per annum
definitions.nfc_new_lending_rate_pct: Total interest rate on new lei-denominated loans to non-financial corporations, percent per annum
definitions.household_new_lending_rate_pct: Total interest rate on new lei-denominated loans to households/NPISH, percent per annum

calibration.reason: frozen before estimation; deliberately contains no policy-rate change, making lack of driver variation visible rather than hiding it

structural_selection.reason: contains the July/August 2024 policy easing and is used for rolling-origin diagnostics and baseline comparison

evaluation_holdout.reason: kept untouched until model form and structural-selection judgement are fixed; small size makes any evaluation low-power

holdout_policy.rule: Any future revision informed by these three observations must use a new temporal holdout for independent evaluation.

known_limitations: The frozen public sample is only 13 monthly observations and contains only two policy-rate reductions.
New-business lending rates are volatile and are not effective rates on outstanding loan stocks.
Policy-rate changes are endogenous policy decisions; the sample cannot establish a causal monetary-policy effect.
The calibration segment has a constant policy rate and therefore cannot separately identify long-run pass-through from the intercept in the three-parameter partial-adjustment model.
No seasonal adjustment or exogenous control is introduced because the sample is too small to support a larger specification without worsening identifiability.
transformations: No rescaling beyond retaining published percentage-point units.
For one-step prediction, the previous observed lending rate is used exactly as available at each origin.
